anomaly_def.Name: Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly: Engine-level runtime settings (memory pools, checkpoint cadence, log size, parallelism, etc.) are mis-tuned relative to hardware capacity and workload demands.
Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly: The generation, flushing, or archival of write-ahead log records becomes the principal bottleneck on the write path.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly: On-disk pages or index structures become physically or logically corrupt, rendering access paths and checksums unreliable.

When these three root causes manifest together, the system may exhibit a confusing blend of symptoms: 1) commit latency and log-flush waits surge while overall I/O and CPU metrics appear under-utilised; 2) sudden checkpoint storms, repeated log-file switches, or archiver backlogs coincide with query plans unexpectedly falling back to full table scans or returning inconsistent row counts; 3) integrity-check utilities report page or index corruption just as background workers throttle or stall due to mis-sized memory pools and aggressive checkpoint parameters; 4) application workloads experience intermittent dead-time where writes hang, followed by bursts of redo, page-verification errors, and emergency auto-recovery cycles.

Causal interaction: Mis-configured memory and checkpoint parameters can inflate redo generation rates and shrink log-buffer headroom, quickly pushing the transaction-log subsystem into saturation. Prolonged log pressure delays checkpoint completion and increases dirty-page residency, making any latent page or index corruption more likely to surface during forced flushes or crash-recovery cycles. Conversely, the presence of corrupted pages triggers extra recovery and validation work, amplifying log-write volume and stressing both the mis-configured buffers and the already constrained log path. The three factors therefore reinforce one another: bad parameters create excess log traffic, log saturation prolongs exposure to corrupt data pages, and corruption events in turn force additional I/O and recovery processing, all of which feed back into the mis-tuned configuration and exacerbate throughput collapse and data-quality risks.

entry.official_description: Found existing redo log files, but at least one is missing. It is unknown if recovery could reach physically consistent state. Please consider restoring from backup or providing --innodb-force-recovery > 0.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with file creation, filesystem access, write durability, log persistence, tablespace management, or storage-capacity boundaries.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect filesystem capacity and permissions, verify persistence paths, review log and data placement, and check whether storage latency or write failures are affecting the engine.
